chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

We were at a funeral, and in front of us was a donkey that urinated. Then the wind brought its urine until it struck our faces and our clothes. So we went in to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and informed him, and he said: There is no harm upon you.

key_terms.جَنَازَةٍ: a funeral procession or funeral setting
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm or problem upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if donkey urine is blown by the wind onto a person's face or clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a question put to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about donkey urine carried by the wind onto people's faces and clothes during a funeral. He replied that there was no harm upon them, indicating a ruling of ritual purity and no liability in this circumstance.
